scope: First deliberately cross-regional weak-coverage batch after cartography/release foundations: Southeast Asia, Americas, Oceania/Pacific, East/Southern Africa, plus a West/Central African external-network candidate.
selection_basis: Canonical v0.6.1 research-management coverage matrix identifies Oceania/Pacific, Americas, West/Central Africa, East/Southern Africa and Southeast Asia among the weakest broad regions. These scores guided research priority only; they were not used as historical prevalence evidence.
cases: Funan — recurrent enslavement in exogenous Chinese textual tradition, P2, geometry unresolved
Southern Maya Lowlands — recurrent Late Classic captive-taking/incorporation, P2, not a blanket slavery claim
Hawaiian Islands — hereditary kauwā status represented as other servile dependency, P3, small scale explicitly preserved
Songo Mnara — positive fifteenth-century site-level slavery designation with practice_level intentionally NULL because intensity is not defensible from the archaeological evidence
external_network_candidates: Eighth-century central-Saharan / Zaghāwa-Kawār slave traffic — preserve for future external-participation ingestion; no territorial P-level assigned
unresolved_issues: Funan is an exogenous Chinese historical category with debated political geography. Resolve any geometry in narrower bounded slices; modern Cambodia/Vietnam and maximum-extent reconstructions are not acceptable substitutes.
The Funan textual witnesses are not automatically independent simply because multiple later Chinese histories preserve similar material.
The Late Classic Maya case records captive-taking/incorporation, not blanket slavery. Prisoners had varied outcomes and captive iconography is not a prevalence metric.
The Maya case spans multiple polities and therefore remains geometry-unresolved at regional level.
Kauwā is retained as a context-sensitive indigenous status category under other_servile_dependency. P3 reflects hereditary institutional structure, not demographic scale.
The Hawaiʻi case predates complete political unification; do not apply later kingdom or modern state geometry to the whole interval.

Songo Mnara has a positive specialist slavery interpretation, but proposed material proxies are ambiguous. Practice intensity remains NULL rather than forcing P1 from an archaeological argument that does not securely measure recurrence.
Do not generalize Songo Mnara to the entire medieval Swahili coast.
The Zaghāwa/Kawār evidence belongs to an external/network lane until bounded territorial-status evidence is established.
No case in this batch is published or part of a release.
next_research: Continue the weak-region strategy rather than returning automatically to Mediterranean/Atlantic source-dense areas.
Seek bounded pre-1500 West/Central African territorial-status evidence independent of trans-Saharan export reports.
Expand Oceania/Pacific beyond Hawaiʻi with source-specific status research rather than pan-Polynesian analogy.
For the Americas, add non-Maya cases and keep captive-taking, tribute, labor obligations and slavery analytically separate.
For Southeast Asia, test other early documentary/epigraphic regions without projecting later Angkorian or colonial categories backward.
For East/Southern Africa, build additional site/polity-specific cases before any coast-wide synthesis.
Resolve geometry only after the historical target and temporal slice are defensible under D-055.
